newsitem.title: INDIA: Fire out at Indian Oil Corp refinery.
newsitem.headline: Fire out at Indian Oil Corp refinery.

text.p: A fire broke which broke out at Indian Oil Corp's refinery at Haldia in West Bengal was brought under control early on Monday, an IOC official said.
The official said crude oil tank number 106 at the 3.75 million tonne refinery caught fire at 6.55 a.m (0125 GMT) on Sunday. The blaze was brought under control by 7.07 a.m on Monday.
"There was no damage since the crude tank was not in operation after its last closing on July 13. Only a protion of the seal of the tank was damaged," he said.

The official said there was little crude oil stored at the refinery because of lower crude supplies over the past four months. "Due to inclement weather, the berthing of ships at Haldia port had become difficult, and due to a slippage in supplies, refinery throughput had been cut down since July 15."
The official said the fire was apparently triggered by a lightning hit.
